text:
maya: Quick checkpoint — Q2 runtime roadmap. I want to lock scope for kernels/quant/KV work this week so PM + infra can finalize capacity buys. High level: 1) kernel refactor for fused attention (low risk) 2) quantization profiles for 7B/13B (medium risk) 3) KV cache autotune + prefix caching experiments (unknown risk). Thoughts?

liam: +1 on locking scope. question: do we treat quant as experimental opt-in or default for Dedicated?

sara: From support/CS: several customers asked for deterministic latency under load — they care more about KV cache improvements and can tolerate quant as opt-in.

oliver: Kernel refactor removes the old aten path, needs ~3 sprint effort but reduces p95 by ~12% on internal bench (r4). Will require coordinating ops for canary nodes.

maya: Good — so prioritization signals: customer asks (latency determinism) > infra cost savings > broad model coverage. That suggests KV+kernels first, quant as follow-up opt-in. Agree?

noah: Minor counter: quant reduces token cost ~25% which is a major sales metric for hosted. If we postpone, we lose operational cost leverage in next quarter. Can we parallel some quant profiling work without making it GA?

liam: Proposal: split quant work into (A) offline profile + regression harness (1 sprint) (B) GA rollout (2-3 sprints) so we can start (A) now in parallel to kernels.

maya: I like that. Launch criteria (for each initiative):
- kernels: p95 latency reduction >= 8% on primary 8k workload, no increase in error rates, rollout canary to 5% traffic then 25% with auto-fallback.
- KV cache autotune: stable hit-rate improvement >= 15% on prefix-heavy traffic, no high memory churn, must have metrics and backfill script.
- quant (opt-in): end-to-end quality delta <= 1.5% BLEU-like eval on our prompt set for each model, cost reduction >= 15% on quantized path, and memory/regression tests.

kai: Can we add an SLO for jitter? Customers are calling out 95th vs 99th. Suggest we track p99 change separately for kernels and mark p99 guardrail: no regression >5%.

maya: Added. Also we should capture rollback triggers: any increase in client error-rate >0.5% absolute or RL dataset regressions flagged by evals.

deploy-bot: Deploy request queued: kernels/refactor branch -> staging at 2023-11-03T09:00Z.

oliver: FYI: staging perf looks promising but we still see a regressing microbench on long-sequence decoder. Need to investigate attention ordering.

liam: Action items: (1) liam + oliver to split kernel refactor into phased PRs and doc canary plan (2) noah + sara to kickoff quant profiling jobpack and eval harness (3) maya to update roadmap slide with launch criteria and capacity ask by Thurs EOD.

maya: If anyone has objections to this ordering speak now, else I'll mark KV+kernels top priority and quant opt-in profile as parallel starter. :thumbsup:

noah: :thumbsup: on plan. I'll attach initial quant profiles to the ticket later today.

oliver: I'll post canary checklist and staging perf snapshot in the PR.

maya: Thanks — closing this thread after roadmap doc update.
